official instructions
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions.
Check compatibility
Connect to the Wi-Fi network of your OpenWrt router. For first pairing, turn off any active VPN on your phone. If Android asks for local-network access, grant permission.
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions.
Install a compatible FoxHole OpenWrt Client using the official instructions, or use the in-app setup wizard (beta) to install the package on a supported router.
After installing the package manually, open LuCI → Services → FoxHole and set the owner PIN if it has not been configured. There is no preset PIN.
Open Router in the app. Find the router or enter its private local address, tap Connect and enter the PIN.

FoxHole does not install or update OpenWrt firmware. You need your own VPN profile or provider subscription. Manage the router VPN in the web panel or a FoxHole app. Open FoxHole OpenWRT at the router address; use the web panel button to switch between FoxHole and LuCI.
Profiles, exported configurations and subscription URLs may contain access secrets. Share them only with people and routers you trust. Transfer is not continuous two-way profile synchronization.

In the router settings, enable “Home VPN server” and confirm the action. Router → phone: open VPN clients, create a client profile and tap IMPORT TO PHONE. The inbound VPN profile connects the phone to the home router, where the current routing rules apply. This requires a configured inbound Hysteria2 server, a reachable public IPv4 address and a UDP port. A provider’s Static IP service is one suitable option.
Connecting to the router over VPN requires a reachable public IPv4 address and an open UDP port supported by the current configuration. Local and foreign traffic routes are configured in Settings.

Smart disconnects only the active home VPN profile imported from this paired router when you join the confirmed home Wi-Fi network with verified VPN routing. On cellular, it reconnects the same unchanged profile. “Home VPN server” and “Manage over mobile networks” must be enabled. Other profiles, Wi-Fi networks, and manual actions are not overridden. Smart is off by default and requires the monitoring notification. Reconnection starts within 90 seconds after home Wi-Fi is lost, not after VPN disconnects. Manual control or profile changes cancel the transition.
If the router certificate changes, check the device and the cause first. Do not ignore an identity mismatch or bypass certificate verification.
Additional modules can run separately or with supported modes. Availability depends on the protocol and scenario; the app checks compatibility before starting.

Supported rule changes are applied consistently. Changes to capture mode or tunnel settings may require stopping and restarting. If a change is rejected, check the reason and current state; a refusal is not a guarantee that nothing changed.
Tor does not carry UDP. In VPN + Tor, the selected policy sends UDP through VPN or blocks it; VPN-carried UDP does not gain Tor anonymity. Tor-only blocks ordinary UDP; DNS is handled separately.

I2P uses a separate i2pd process and a TCP-only local SOCKS5 route. It requires Guard DNS processing and cannot start with strict Android Private DNS. The I2P lane is unavailable with the current WireGuard/AmneziaWG packet tunnel.
The firewall started by I2P transparent mode does not apply general routing rules: blocking and DNS interception are disabled, and only .i2p traffic is routed.

Notification checks are periodic, not live push. Polling requires its assigned route and verified loopback proxy; WireGuard/AmneziaWG provide no polling bridge. Unavailable routes and failed proxy overrides block polling. Storage isolation depends on WebView support; without multiple profiles, web apps share a profile with origin isolation.

The current WireGuard/AmneziaWG packet path requires numeric profile DNS and has no local DNS interception/filtering. DoQ/DoH3 final resolvers are rejected. If required enabled filter categories cannot be applied, session preparation is refused rather than silently bypassing them.

LAN proxy cannot start with WireGuard/AmneziaWG. Authentication is mandatory; an empty password prevents startup. The local client-to-phone segment has no additional encryption: use trusted Wi-Fi networks only.

Network rules associate a profile with a Wi-Fi network or mobile data. When the network changes, the app can show a local notification suggesting the profile or connect it according to your setting. This does not provide cloud push or bypass Android background limits.

Subscriptions use your saved provider URL. When background refresh is enabled, the default interval is 12 hours; supported profiles can refresh automatically.

FoxHole DB supplies signed data, not executable code. TLS fingerprint tables are checked every 24 hours by default when enabled; installing prepared data needs your action. Other datasets follow their feature settings.
The GitHub build checks for app updates daily. Downloading and installation require your action and Android confirmation. F-Droid updates the F-Droid build.
Tap “+” and choose an available option to import a configuration or an HTTPS provider subscription.
Choose a supported configuration file.
Scan a profile QR code with the camera.
Select the saved profile and, when applicable, the server/protocol option.
Tap Start and approve Android’s system VPN request.
Check the connection state. Stop cancels connecting and disconnects VPN.

Sentinel checks available app information and network indicators. A match or risk signal needs review and does not always mean infection. Static APK scanning is enabled separately; coverage depends on access in Android OS.

Open the finding’s source, confidence and coverage. A static API reference is not proof of execution. Partial, unavailable or unsupported data is not a clean result; no matches means no matches only in the checked area.
Enter a supported connection link manually in the add-profile field.

Phone to router: long-press a saved profile and tap “Send config to router.” A v2rayTun subscription is not transferred in full; only the selected compatible node is sent. You can also tap “+” in the “Manage” header of router management. The app searches all saved profiles and subscriptions for compatible configurations. Select one or more and tap “Transfer.” Only selected nodes are transferred; then choose the profile on the router and start the VPN separately.
A Smart VPN profile combines several VPN protocols for one server into a single list for quick switching and connection testing.

You can test all protocols available in the subscription; this blocks all device traffic, switches the app to whole-device VPN mode, measures three parameters, and restores the last active connection. The ★ icon marks the best connections from the test results.

Settings → Application → App database. Export includes the selected profiles and transferable settings. Encrypt backup is off by default: the file is plaintext and no password is requested. Enable it to create an AES-encrypted file with a password. Profiles may contain access credentials; keep plaintext files private and store encrypted files separately from their passwords. A forgotten password cannot be recovered.

Import detects the format automatically and requests a password only for encrypted files. Review the backup summary and confirm before restoring. Device-local values stay on this device: the FoxHole Guard PIN, update token, OS permissions (Usage Access), generated local-proxy passwords and local FoxHole Sentinel databases.
The same section provides selective clearing of journals, statistics and profiles, plus a complete and irreversible Factory Reset.

Long-press a saved VPN profile to open its management actions: select, rename, edit, or delete. To save or share a saved VPN profile, select it and use the controls below. Sharing through a QR code is available for a single configuration and v2raytun subscriptions. The “+” button in VPN Profiles creates a new configuration from a blank template with a selectable protocol type.\nIn a Smart profile, each protocol is stored as an isolated entry and configured independently.\nSecurity: connections without certificate verification (Insecure TLS/AllowInsecure) require explicit user confirmation; this permission is stored locally only for the profile being edited.

Supported import formats are a URI copied to the clipboard, a configuration file, and a scanned QR code. When a subscription profile in v2raytun format is added, FoxHole Guard updates it automatically before connecting. Long-press START to update the subscription manually without connecting. Multi-select mode lets you select several profiles for batch export to a file. A single profile or protocol can be shared as a URI or QR code.

What is checked
How to run
Understanding results
Monitoring
Privacy and coverage
Expert static-check settings
In the Sentinel journal or static-check settings, choose an installed app in “Choose an application”. Only apps visible to Android OS can be selected.
Use “Check selected app” for that app or “Check installed apps” for the currently visible apps. “Cancel check” cancels the request; skipped and incomplete checks remain explicit.

When a report is available, “View this report” opens that exact report. Saved scan history is encrypted and bounded; clearing it needs confirmation. Cached results keep their original scan date. Unsaved or deferred-journal results are identified.

Collection status and confidence are independent. Declared capability, enabled component and granted access are different observations; unknown stays unknown. An exposure is not a threat verdict. A completed scan covers bounded APK/DEX data, not native execution, dynamic behavior or the whole device.

FoxHole Sentinel analyzes available OS and network metadata. It does not inspect traffic payloads. A risk signal or an unfamiliar installation source does not prove malicious code. App checks use installation identity, requested capabilities, available signing certificates and the enabled indicator lists. The stalkerware baseline comes from AssoEchap/stalkerware-indicators under CC-BY-4.0.

Unchanged installation metadata reuses cached signer facts. App-change bursts are processed in bounded batches; incomplete package visibility is not treated as removal or a clean result. When password protection and event monitoring are enabled, a sealed hash-chained journal records observed installations, updates, removals and monitoring gaps. Queue gaps are reported explicitly.

Passive network IOC matching is separate from optional full network history. Per-app network ownership needs Android 10 or later and is not available for every short or shared-UID flow. Background traffic and country analysis retain separate opt-in controls.

Economy uses events and system-scheduled repair without a permanent foreground host. Reinforced adds a foreground service and notification. Neither mode bypasses Android Doze or guarantees an exact repair interval. Force-stop, root access and system app-data clearing remain outside FoxHole Sentinel control. No measured battery-saving percentage is implied.

Static APK checks are optional and run in a separate isolated process. Select an installed app or check the apps currently visible to Android. Open Expert static-check settings in Sentinel settings for DEX references, YARA rules, finding notifications, automatic new or updated app checks, charging and battery constraints, and the 16 or 64 MiB artifact budget. Heavy and automatic checks default off. Critical or unknown battery state and low storage pause scans. Cancel, policy changes and app replacement prevent outdated results from being published. Incomplete checks stay partial and are not cached as complete. The bundled rules report static API references; a MITRE candidate mapping does not prove that a technique ran. Locked journals defer results until unlock; optional finding notifications use a shared cooldown.
The package supports VLESS, Hysteria2, and WireGuard clients. Incoming connections use a separate Hysteria2 server module.
Profiles, exported configurations and subscription addresses may contain access secrets. Share them only with trusted people and routers. You can delete a VPN client profile at any time.
